The rooftop herb garden began as three pots on the parapet and now
covers most of the ledge. Rosemary and thyme take the baking side,
mint wants the shade by the water tank, and basil wants both and
survives neither.

Wind is the real gardener here. Anything taller than a hand snaps in
the spring gusts, which is why the fennel has never made a second
season, however carefully it is staked.

The aphids arrived before the ladybirds did, and a colony can strip a
basil plant in a week. The bees visit every morning, but they come from
someone else's hives three streets over, and they take the pollen
without asking.
